Only evidence is the Apple album 'Haba, Axman, Novak: String Quartets' (Novak Quartet, Supraphon 2025): tracks 1-3, a three-movement 'String Quartet No. 3' (23:13), but the album gives no first name or year. IMSLP lists only Karel Haba's Quartet No. 2, Op. 5; no source lists his No. 3. Alois Haba's No. 3 (Op. 12) is a two-movement quarter-tone work of about 20 min, so it is not that track.

note: Gyrowetz Op. 14/23/28 trio numbers rest on the recording's track titles only (doubt). Haas SQ 6 was wrongly timed from a festival box that holds other composers' quartets. Hadley Op. 132 is a string quartet on IMSLP and Wikipedia; the piano trio carries that number only on the Albany disc. Karel Haba No. 3 is unverifiable beyond one album. Halffter SQ 1 is the Three Pieces on the MDG disc but en.wikipedia lists both separately.
